object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: Anyone in the system, identified by a person ID.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: Employee
object_types.definition: A Person who is an employee; identified the same way as Person.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.
A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

object_types.name: Department
object_types.definition: An organizational unit identified by a department code, with a unique department name.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.
Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: DepartmentName
object_types.definition: The name of a Department, e.g. 'Payroll' or 'Field Operations'. Unique across departments.

source_references.excerpt: Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether a Department can be managed by more than one Manager simultaneously, or whether managing a Department implies the manager also works in that department. The transcript states managers manage at most one department but does not clarify if department-to-manager is one-to-one or one-to-many, nor whether management role is mandatory for departments (can a department have no manager at all?).

ambiguities.description: The reference mode for Employee and Manager is stated to be the same as Person (person_id), meaning these subtypes do not have independent identifiers. This is consistent with subtype identification sharing, but it's worth confirming that no separate 'employee number' or 'manager number' exists, since only Person ID was mentioned.
